1.explanation:
• MultiSelect/MultiSelect.mdx and README.md: show how selected items render as filter tags and how the component wraps everything in a button role container. 
• Tag/Tag.mdx: documents the Tag component’s "filter" type which renders as a button for removability—this is the nested interactive element.  
• Button/Button.mdx: provides context on the HTML <button> element and accessibility guidelines around interactive content.  
• ListBox/README.md: explains the underlying ListBox structure (a button role wrapper) used by MultiSelect, clarifying why nesting Tag’s button creates the spec violation.  
Together, these documents illustrate how MultiSelect, Tag, and ListBox combine to produce a nested-button scenario and guide where changes must be made to prevent an interactive descendant inside a button.
1.bug_scenario: When a user selects items in the MultiSelect control, each selected item is rendered as a removable Tag (filter token) inside the main MultiSelect button wrapper. The outer wrapper is a <div role="button" …> representing the combobox, and each Tag filter is itself implemented as a <button> (with the “×” clear‐selection icon). This results in an interactive <button> nested inside another interactive element (the MultiSelect’s button role), violating the HTML5 spec requirement that “there must be no interactive content descendant” within a <button>. The provided DOM screenshot highlights the outer host (in green) and the nested clear‐selection button (in yellow), and the UI screenshot shows the two selected tags and the dropdown arrow.
